audit.why: 52.99% over 2089 games. Sett owns the resistance-poor early game; K'Sante takes over once two tank items and All Out are online. EVEN / 6/10 with carry threat 7/10 matches. Note the mirror recorded 1281 games and 50.74% from its packet — the sample differs between files but the shape of the lane does not.
audit.corrected: Sett-favoured lane, K'Sante-favoured late. Difficulty 6/10 stands.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Sett/Sett/Sett/Skill/Sett/Skill/Skill. The mirror already settled rows 4-6 as Skill / Sett / K'Sante, and the packet gives Sett levels 4-5. whys[6] on this very page says K'Sante 'eclipses your dueling' at two-plus items while win[6] said Skill.
audit.why: Packet and mirror agree, and the content whys already argue the corrected owners for rows 3, 5 and 6. Level 6 is genuinely even: All Out heals and transforms him for 120s, so a naked Show Stopper is not a free win.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Sett / Sett / Sett / Sett / Skill / Sett / K'Sante in both layers, ratings re-scaled, and the whys that named the wrong owner at level 6 and levels 4-5 rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and two mechanics that decide every trade were missing: Path Maker's charge-up reduces the damage he takes and its hit deals true damage, and Footwork gives him a shield on a 10s cooldown that eats a cashed Haymaker.
audit.why: Riot's text: W 'charges up, taking reduced damage, then dashes, knocking back and stunning' — flagged trueDamage, so stacking armour reads the trade wrong. E 'dashes and gains a shield', 10s at rank 1. Q is 3.5s and pulls at 2 stacks. R is 120s at rank 1 and grants healing while cutting his defences.
audit.corrected: Trade after Path Maker's charge (14s at rank 1), not into it — it reduces his damage taken and lands true damage. Bait Footwork's 10s shield before cashing grit. All Out: 120s, heals him, so Grievous Wounds before extended fights.

audit.whatIsWrong: Executioner's Calling is listed in report[8] with the reason 'his healing out-paces your grit trades', but no field ties the healing to All Out, and armour is implied as the answer to a kit that deals true damage through Path Maker.
audit.why: All Out is the only healing source in his kit and it is on 120s; Path Maker's true damage means Plated Steelcaps and armour stacking are not the counter the page implies.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds is for All Out specifically; armour does nothing against Path Maker's true damage.

edits.before: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier, but K'Sante has his core tools too. Keep the grit bar honest: trade in, W-shield his return damage, out.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay yours: Footwork's shield is 10s at rank 1, so bait it out, bank grit off his poke, then cash Haymaker on the naked follow-up.

edits.before: The Show Stopper online — you can start fights K'Sante doesn't want. Suplex him into your wave or tower, never into his own minions.
edits.after: Level 6 is a read — All Out heals him and reshapes his kit for 120s. Suplex him into your wave only once Footwork's shield is spent.

edits.before: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Fights are decided by whether you cash a max-grit W — track All Out and commit on the gap.
edits.after: Two tank items in, All Out's healing and his shred beat you in a straight duel — take fights with your jungler or a numbers edge, not alone.

edits.before: - K'Sante All Out: matchup-defining — His duelist mode. All-in when it’s down. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - All Out (R): 120s at rank 1 — it heals him and drops his defences. - Path Maker (W): 14s, true damage.

edits.before: Your level 6 R outperforms his — it displaces and carries without needing setup.
edits.after: Level 6 is a read: both ults flip the fight, and All Out heals him through yours.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 are your window — E Facebreaker into Q lets you land W Haymaker with the full slow-empowered payload before he has Sunfire and tabis. Your R displaces him regardless of his tankiness, so all-in when his W is on cooldown and you're ahead on Grit.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 are your window — Facebreaker into Q lets you cash Haymaker before he has Sunfire and tabis. Path Maker's charge reduces the damage he takes and its hit is true damage, so trade after it, not into it, and buy Grievous Wounds before he can heal through All Out.
